page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Mericarp — definition
lines: The one-seeded pieces into which a
schizocarpic dry fruit splits are called
steps.why: A mericarp is defined THROUGH the schizocarpic fruit - it is the one-seeded unit produced by the split.
common_mistakes: Calling a mericarp a seed. It is a piece of the FRUIT that contains one seed.
steps.memory_tip: Meri - part; carp - fruit: one part of a split fruit.
steps.margin_note: One sentence linking mericarp to the schizocarpic split.

steps.label: Plants

lines.text: Found in Acacia and castor; also in

lines: coriander, whose cremocarp splits into two
steps.why: The book names Acacia and castor (its schizocarpic examples); coriander is the classic textbook case - a cremocarp splitting into exactly two mericarps.
common_mistakes: Naming plants with capsules (cotton, Datura). Capsules release seeds; they do not break into mericarps.
steps.memory_tip: The two halves of a coriander split are two mericarps.
steps.margin_note: The book's pair (Acacia, castor) is enough; coriander strengthens it.
